SEPARATION AGREEMENT AND GENERAL RELEASE
DRAFT 3 - F&A comments 05/11/2026 - PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - NOT FOR EXECUTION
This Separation Agreement and General Release (the "Agreement") is entered into between Brightwater Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal office at 3300 Arapahoe Parkway, Suite 410, Boulder, Colorado 80303 (the "Company"), and Jordan A. Paris ("Employee"), residing at 918 Juniper Court, Unit B, Longmont, CO 80501-4420.
1. Separation
Employee's employment as Senior Data Engineer (Employee ID BW-004471) will end effective May 29, 2026 (the "Separation Date"). Employee was hired on August 14, 2017. The Company will pay all wages earned through the Separation Date and accrued, unused paid time off in the gross amount of $3,912.44, whether or not Employee signs this Agreement.
2. Severance
In exchange for the release in Section 4, the Company will pay Employee severance of $48,750.00, equal to thirteen weeks of base salary, less applicable withholdings, reported on Form W-2. Payment will be made by direct deposit to the account on file ending in 2205 within ten business days after the Effective Date. The Company will also pay the employer share of COBRA premiums under the Front Range Mutual Health Plan (member no. FRM-88204417-01) through November 30, 2026, estimated at $1,187.20 per month. The parties intend that payments be exempt from Section 409A.
3. Pending Charge
Employee filed Charge No. 541-2026-01447 with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission on March 3, 2026, alleging that the Company denied his request for a reduced schedule to accommodate multiple sclerosis and selected him for layoff because of his age. The Company denies these allegations. Employee agrees to request withdrawal of the charge within five days after the Effective Date. Nothing in this Agreement prevents Employee from communicating with any government agency or from exercising rights under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act.
4. General Release
Employee releases the Company and its officers, directors and affiliates from all claims arising through the date Employee signs, including claims under Title VII, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act and the Age Discrimination in Employment Act. In compliance with 29 U.S.C. § 626(f), Employee acknowledges that he has been advised in writing to consult an attorney, has been given at least twenty-one (21) days to consider this Agreement, and may revoke it within seven (7) days after signing by written notice to Maribel Ortiz-Vega, Vice President, People, at mortizvega@brightwater-analytics.example.
5. Return of Property
Employee will return by the Separation Date the Company laptop (serial no. C02ZK4QWMD6T), the security token (ID TKN-55-018822) and building badge no. 40127. Employee's network account (jparis) will be disabled at 5:00 p.m. on the Separation Date. Ms. Ortiz-Vega has confirmed that Employee may keep the mobile phone ending 0158 after it is wiped.
6. References; Non-Disparagement
The Company will confirm dates of employment and last position held only. Inquiries are to be directed to M. Ortiz-Vega at (720) 555-0103. Neither party will disparage the other.
7. Attorneys' Fees
The Company will pay $6,500 toward Employee's attorneys' fees directly to Oyelaran Employment Law, L.L.C. (EIN 84-3917720) upon receipt of a Form W-9.
8. Governing Law
This Agreement is governed by Colorado law. Venue lies in the District Court for Boulder County.

Confirm with Brightwater payroll whether the last four of his SSN on the wage statement (xxx-xx-5807) match the file. Oyelaran says they do not.
